title: DID WE MAKE IT?

FIRST_YEAR_SKY.description: Younger Sky, first year at MSRIT, approximately two years younger; asks the questions.

THIRD_YEAR_SKY.description: Current Sky, third year at MSRIT; answers from lived experience, direct then empathetic.

lines.speaker: FIRST_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: So… did we make it?

lines.speaker: THIRD_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: Take this. Read it.

lines.speaker: FIRST_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: It's blank.

lines.speaker: FIRST_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: You used to send me voice notes—ideas, plans, all those thoughts you couldn't switch off. What happened?

lines.speaker: THIRD_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: I don't know how to write the ending yet.

lines.speaker: FIRST_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: Then start at the beginning. Start with college.

lines.speaker: THIRD_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: I came from Gokak. I was quiet, a little shy. I chose Bengaluru because startups were everywhere.

lines.speaker: FIRST_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: I thought we'd be building a company straight away.

lines.speaker: THIRD_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: I wanted to build something big. I looked up to Elon Musk. I thought: start small, keep scaling.

lines.speaker: FIRST_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: Okay. So what did we actually build?

lines.speaker: THIRD_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: For almost a year, I mostly thought. I asked AI if my ideas were good. I had more plans than proof.

lines.speaker: FIRST_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: What finally got us moving?

lines.speaker: THIRD_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: A conversation with friends about a hackathon problem. I built a first version in four or five hours, learning what I needed as I went.

lines.speaker: FIRST_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: Four hours? Seriously?

lines.speaker: THIRD_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: I bought a domain two days later. Sent ten emails. One person replied.

lines.speaker: FIRST_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: One reply. That must've felt huge.

lines.speaker: THIRD_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: It did. It was about website content licensing and stopping AI scrapers. But I'd chosen the wrong customers: small publishers didn't feel enough pain; bigger ones already had solutions.

lines.speaker: FIRST_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: So you changed direction?

lines.speaker: THIRD_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: First LLM budget enforcement. Then agent governance. That one took five months. I learned TypeScript, Python, React and Redis while building it.
lines.delivery: measured, quietly proud of the learning

lines.speaker: FIRST_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: You learned all that. Did people start using it?

lines.speaker: THIRD_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: I sent around fifty emails. Zero replies.

lines.speaker: FIRST_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: Didn't you try other ways?

lines.speaker: THIRD_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: Two Dev.to articles, Reddit, Twitter. One security post took off—then moderators removed it because my account was new.

lines.speaker: FIRST_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: So did we make any money?

lines.speaker: THIRD_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: Zero. I imagined five thousand dollars a month by December. Placements were getting closer, too.

lines.speaker: FIRST_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: Was I wrong to dream that big?

lines.speaker: THIRD_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: No. You got us started. After two months away, I learned: real problems come from people, not prompts.
lines.delivery: warm, empathetic, direct to the younger self

lines.speaker: THIRD_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: I'm exploring physical AI.

lines.speaker: FIRST_YEAR_SKY
lines.text: Let's go.
